evidence.statement: Frozen exact-word calibration establishes a usable cross-domain signal boundary at k=14-16 and a composition-dominated regime at k=12.
The A2451-centered missing-code search produced zero all-three exact target tokens at both k=16 and separately preregistered k=14.

MOP16-14-v1 is a prospective decompiler representation that keeps the 14-base specificity floor while permitting two variable positions in a 16-base span; its biological usefulness is UNKNOWN until the frozen global/null test is executed.
MOP16-14-v1 produced 618,470 distinct three-domain shared token types versus five exact-dinucleotide-preserving null counts 421,985; 417,911; 421,935; 425,242; and 423,492.
The real global count is 1.4652x the null mean and 1.4544x the maximum null count; all 120 individual masks separately exceed their own five-null maximum.

Allowing two variable positions while preserving 14 exact positions in a fixed 16-nt span recovers a broad cross-domain recurrence layer that remains strongly separated from composition-preserving nulls.

semantics.validated_identity: annotation-blind representation with positive global null separation

unknowns: Which subsets of the 618,470 masked token types map to coherent biological structures after candidate freeze.
How MOP transfer behaves across independent organism sets and evolutionary depths.
Whether more expressive variable-slot representations improve held-out description without losing null separation.
